title: Locally finite codimension-one cycles and principality at a point
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A locally finite codimension-one cycle is a function $n:X\to\mathbf Z$, zero away from points $z$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], such that the family of closed sets $\overline{\{z\}}$ for $n(z)\ne0$ is locally finite. Equivalently its support $\{z:n(z)\ne0\}$ is locally finite (Stacks Tag 02QR, algebraic cycles): an open set meets $\overline{\{z\}}$ exactly when it contains $z$. These closures are the nonempty irreducible closed subsets [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic points $z$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Thus this is the locally finite formal sum $\sum_z n(z)[\overline{\{z\}}]$, with zero terms omitted. Now suppose $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], fix $x\in X$, and suppose $R_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For each height-one prime $q$ of $R_x$ [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group], let $z_q$ be its image under the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R_x\to X$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. The cycle is principal at $x$ if some $a\in\operatorname{Frac}(R_x)^\times$ satisfies $v_q(a)=n(z_q)$ for every such $q$, using the normalized fraction order [def-trf-height-one-fraction-order].
